reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20 agent-U: the prior Batch 102 edit was a no-op (kept answer key unchanged) and left the question stem incoherent. The stem says 'the latest Revised IRR of RA 9184' but every option references 'RA 12009' as if it were an IRR. RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, signed 20 July 2024) is a NEW STATUTE that REVISED/REPEALED RA 9184, not an IRR of RA 9184. The previous rationale's phrase 'Updated 2016 Revised IRR of RA 9184 (as of July 2024)' is wrong because July 2024 is the date RA 12009 was signed, not an IRR update. Rewrote so the stem, options, and rationale consistently describe RA 12009 as the successor statute and ask the source-safe takeaway (architects should track the new law and its IRR and PhilGEPS e-procurement).

proposed.text: What is the source-safe framing of RA 12009 (signed 20 July 2024) relative to RA 9184, and what should architects do?

options.text: RA 12009 is a new Implementing Rules and Regulations updating RA 9184; architects only need to re-read the old IRR
RA 12009 is a new statute (New Government Procurement Act) that revises RA 9184; architects should track the new law, its IRR, and PhilGEPS e-procurement requirements
RA 12009 repeals all procurement rules so architects no longer need to bid for government work
RA 12009 only applies to private architectural projects, so government architects can ignore it

rationale.a: RA 12009 is not an IRR; it is a new statute that revises RA 9184 itself.
rationale.b: RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act of 2024, signed 20 July 2024) is a successor statute that revises RA 9184. Architects should follow the new law, its IRR, and the PhilGEPS e-procurement system.
rationale.c: RA 12009 revises rather than abolishes government procurement; bidding rules remain, modernized.
rationale.d: RA 12009 applies to government procurement, not private projects; government-side architects must follow it.
rationale.correct: RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act of 2024, signed 20 July 2024) is a successor statute that revises RA 9184. Architects should follow the new law, its IRR, and the PhilGEPS e-procurement system.
rationale.takeaway: Do not conflate a statute with an IRR. RA 12009 is the new law; its IRR is a separate instrument. Track both plus PhilGEPS for e-procurement.

proposed.explanation: RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act of 2024, signed 20 July 2024) is a successor statute that revises RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003). It is not an IRR of RA 9184. Architects working on government projects should follow the new law, its Implementing Rules and Regulations, and the PhilGEPS e-procurement platform.
